processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Five Cu molds moved stepwise inside the furnace; successively filled with melt from a 4-kg ingot; after each cast the remaining melt composition was adjusted by charging Al through an air lock.
10 × 50 × 130 mm³ blocks hot rolled into 2 ± 0.1 mm thick and ~500 mm long sheets.
Cut perpendicular to the rolling direction into sets of nine segments with dimensions 2 × 60 × 55 mm³ for each alloy composition.
One of the aging treatments (450/500/550/600 °C for 0/1/24 h) in the 45-condition RAP matrix; this sample is the 500 °C / 1 h condition.
Scales were removed from the surfaces by low-pressure, fine-grit sandblasting after the heat treatments.

structures.overall_structure: Single-phase austenitic (fcc) fully recrystallized microstructure; low-density SIMPLEX TWIP steel with ~20 µm grain size and some retained Mn microsegregations.

unmapped_findings: The Fe-30Mn-1.2C-2Al sample aged 500 °C for 1 h belongs to the 45-condition RAP matrix (5 alloys × 9 heat treatments) screened within 35 h.

For the Fe-30Mn-1.2C system, alloys with intermediate Al contents (2–6 wt.%) have properties between the Al-free and 8 wt.% Al variants, and show only a much smaller influence of aging on tensile behavior; pronounced aging strengthening (attributed to nm-sized κ-carbides) occurs mainly at ~8 wt.% Al.
The 2 wt.% Al alloy is below the 5 wt.% Al threshold, so a single austenite phase prevails at room temperature and the TWIP effect dominates as the deformation mechanism (SIMPLEX steel).

Al promotes the formation of L′1₂-type κ-carbide nanoprecipitates upon aging with approximate stoichiometry (Fe,Mn)₃AlC, but no κ-carbide data specific to the 2Al/500 °C/1 h sample is reported in the text.

A temperature-sensitive constitutive strain-hardening model for single-phase low-density TWIP (SIMPLEX) steels is described in the paper, but its parameters and validation (Fig. 7) refer to a Fe-22Mn-0.6C model alloy, not this sample.
